slides.title: Introduction BEV Battery Electric Vehicle It’s a Pure Electric Vehicle where the only traction device is the Electric Mo
slides.body:
It’s a Pure Electric Vehicle where the only traction device is the Electric Motor.
The Electric Motor only uses chemical energy supplied by Rechargeable Battery
Packs.
BEV main components are:
1. Electric Machine
2. Battery Packs
3. Power Managing Units
4. Digital Control System

slides.title: Electric Machine Electric Motor
slides.body:
o Since the motor is an electric one, there is NO transmission.
o When the electric motor starts moving, it provides all the drive
torque (it can reach engine speeds > 10000 rpm) with a proper
velocity, without the need for any gear ratio.
o This is the reason why it doesn’t need reverse gear as well! It is
enough to reverse the motor current phase to make it operating
in the opposite direction.
o So, the only two commands to drive it:
1. Gas Pedal
2. Brake Pedal
o

slides.title: Regenerative Braking Alternator Electric Machine
slides.body:
When the driver presses the brake pedal, the discs and the brake pads create
friction as they meet. In turn, the friction creates kinetic energy that dissipates
into the environment in the form of heat.
Regenerative braking recovers some of the kinetic energy that would
otherwise turn into heat; the electric motor reverses its operation, starts
working as an alternator and converts the kinetic energy into electric current;
There are two conditions for regeneration occurrence:
1. The driver applies the brake pedal 🡪 Regenerative Braking
2. The driver releases the accelerator pedal, and the vehicle is coasting 🡪
E-Pedal Functionality or One-Pedal-Drive
The amount of electricity the system generates is proportional to the level of
braking force; the stronger the braking force, the greater the electrical current.
Ultimately, the amount of energy the system captures is dependent on the
vehicle's speed and the duration of brake application.
In order to save energy and make the HV battery charge as long-lasting as possible,
it is essential to take advantage of the bi-directional operation of the electric motor.
AlternatorElectric Machine

slides.title: E-Pedal Functionality Alternator Electric Machine
slides.body:
The E-Pedal (or One Pedal Drive) functionality it’s a extension of the Regenerative Braking
concept broadened to the gas pedal release.
When the driver releases the accelerator pedal, the electric motor reverses its
operation and starts working as an alternator.
It converts the rotational kinetic energy at wheel level into electric current;
Electric current to recharge the HV Battery Pack.
This means energy dissipation at torque level; practically, the vehicle slows
down until it stops.
This is the reason why it is also called ONE PEDAL DRIVE; when the E-Pedal
functionality is on, the driver doesn’t need the brake pedal to stop the vehicle.
It’s enough to release the accelerator pedal and, depending on the current
vehicle speed and the slackening on the gas pedal, the vehicle coast down will
be modulate, stopping the vehicle and giving motion to the alternator by
mechanical energy.
AlternatorElectric Machine

slides.title: Battery System Battery Packs
slides.body:
o An electric vehicle battery (EVB, also known as a traction
battery) is an High Voltage rechargeable battery used to
power the electric motors. The most common battery type
in modern electric vehicles are lithium-ion batteries
because of their high energy density compared to their
weight. All-electric cars have battery capacities between
6.0 kWh (2012 Renault Twizy) and 100 kWh (2012 Tesla
Model S and 2015 Tesla Model X).
o However, every electric vehicle has another Low Voltage
auxiliar battery; Usually, it is a 12V battery used to power
most of vehicle actuators and all the vehicle control units.
It takes its charge from the HV Battery which is the only
one directly connected to the grid (passing by the Onboard
Charger)

Power Managing Units Power Electronics
slides.body:
BEV Power Electronics include all the components between the Electric Motor and the Battery Pack
used to regulate (as a filter) the energy transmission based on the instantaneous energy demand.
Main components are:
- Inverter: a high-power DC to AC converter for the
battery to power the traction motor
- Onboard Charger: an AC - DC rectifier to charge
the battery from the electric grid
- DC-DC Converter: for the high-voltage traction
battery to power a low-voltage battery (tipically, a
12V Battery for hotel facilities and ECU systems)
Most critical of all is the main inverter, which operates
at the highest power and facilitates traction.

slides.title: Digital Control System Main Control Units
slides.body:
Every Battery Electric Vehicle has some really typical control units:
- PIM (Power Inverter Module): high-power DC to AC converter for the battery to power
the traction motor. It includes:
1. EVCU (Electric Vehicle Control Unit): to manage Propulsion, Devices Temperatures,
Auxiliary Components, Battery Charge, and main vehicle actuators.
2. MCP (Motor Control Processor): to mameters; anage E-Motor kinematic parStarting
from gas & brake pedal press informations, MCP strictly interacts with EVCU to
report the estimated shaft torque for torque compensation.
- IDCM (Integrated Dual Charger Module): it combines an on-board charger (AC\DC
Inverter to charge the vehicle from the electric grid) and DC/DC converter (to convert
the HV electric current in a 12V Electric Current to power the Auxiliary 12V Battery
and all the Control Units) in one
- BPCM (Battery Pack Control Module): it is responsible for the management of critical
features such as Voltage, Temperature and Current monitoring, Battery state of
charge (SoC) and cell balancing of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries.

slides.title: 332 City BEV 332 Drive Styles
slides.body:
As the name suggests, 332 City BEV was
meant to be city car, funny but not sporty.
This is the reason why, the driver can choose
between the following 3 drive styles using a
selector device:
1. NORMAL drive style: to drive everywhere
with good accelerations and a 150 kph
maximum speed
2. RANGE drive style: for city driving, with
slightly slower acceleration and the One-
Pedal-Drive functionality active
3. SHERPA drive style: to preserve the
vehicle Battery SOC, with very slow
acceleration, One-Pedal-Drive active and
80 kph as maximum
